newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank probe focused on training.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank probe focused on training.

text.p: A Florida probe of sales practices in the securities business of NationsBank Corp, which ended with a settlement Tuesday, focused on issues of poor training and lack of supervision, said a lawyer for the state.

"Typically, they were talking people out of a safe investment like a cd (certificate of deposit)" and putting them into investments inconsistent with the customer's past investment history, Mary Leontakianakos, a senior assistant attorney general, said in a telephone interview.
"They were referring bank customers over to their brokerage," with bank employees receiving bonuses for the referrals, she added.
The bonuses in and of themselves were not a problem.
"There were issues of poor training and lack of supervision of these brokers," she said.
The settlement of the Florida civil case stipulated there was no finding that any law had been violated. The case was based on activities that occurred in 1993 and 1994.
NationSecurities, a unit of NationsBank, agreed to pay $850,000 to the state and among other things to conduct a review of its operations and to begin an arbitration process.
